raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

External-linker transfers carry reusable physical page indices. A late
completion cannot distinguish an earlier allocation of page N from a newer
allocation of page N using request, tree-node or process metadata alone.

Closes #45493. A search for open PRs by issue number and by
`page generation external linker allocator` found no matching implementation.

## Modifications

- Add opt-in allocator-issued Full/SWA page generations for token, paged and
  NPU allocation paths. Default serving allocates no ledger.
- Carry one generation per complete page in linker load/offload descriptors;
  default Rust tree-core offloads are enriched by the Python allocator owner.
- Use asynchronous device `index_fill_`/`index_select` and attach a CUDA
  readiness event for another stream. Generation equality is explicitly not a
  physical transfer-termination receipt.
- Preserve legacy positional `PoolTransfer` construction, make the new fields
  keyword-only, reject Mamba/non-CPU-CUDA generation profiles, and keep
  overflow/resize failure-safe.

## Accuracy Tests

No model forward or output semantics change. Source/CPU contract controls:

- allocator/linker/assembler: `91 passed`, `12 subtests passed`
- matching prebuilt SGLang 0.5.22 Rust-extension adapter gate: `1 passed`
- canonical changed-file pre-commit: passed

The local source build of `torch-sys 0.24.0` is blocked before candidate code by
its existing Torch 2.13/C++20 `module(...)` identifier conflict; the prebuilt
0.5.22 extension was used to validate the unchanged six-tuple Rust boundary and
candidate adapter enrichment.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

An H20 / Torch 2.14.1 / CUDA 13 component gate on GPU UUID
`GPU-14c5531e-c52e-712b-8b90-fe7fdad8c172` observed after warm-up:

- `index_fill_` host return: 0.041 ms while a preceding CUDA sleep remained pending
- `index_select` + recorded readiness event: 0.171 ms while the sleep remained pending
- old advanced assignment control: 101 ms and waited for the sleep
- 1,000 enabled generation submissions: 6.31 ms device time
- cross-stream event consumption, generation reuse/stale rejection, and compute
  oracle passed; GPU returned to 0 MiB

This is allocator-primitive evidence, not installed SGLang serving or physical
DMA/RDMA termination qualification.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (API docstrings and descriptor contract updated; no user-facing option is enabled by default.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

AI assistance was used for contract analysis, implementation, testing and
review remediation. The human submitter remains responsible for reviewing and
defending every changed line. This PR remains Draft pending that review and
upstream CI.

+    def _issue_allocation_generations(self, page_ids: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+        """Assign identities to physical pages handed to new writers."""
+        if self._allocation_generations is None:
+            return
+        count = page_ids.numel()
+        if count == 0:
+            return
+        generation = self._next_allocation_generation
+        if generation > torch.iinfo(torch.int64).max:
+            raise RuntimeError("KV page allocation generation exhausted")
+        self._allocation_generations.index_fill_(0, page_ids, generation)
+        self._next_allocation_generation += 1
+
+    def enable_allocation_generations(self) -> None:
+        """Enable page identities for a consumer before serving allocations."""
+        if self._allocation_generations is None:
+            self._allocation_generations = torch.zeros(
+                self.size // self.page_size + 1,
+                dtype=torch.int64,
+                device=self.device,
+            )
+
+    def allocation_generations(self, indices: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor | None:
+        """Snapshot allocator identities for complete physical pages.
+
+        The caller supplies complete page-aligned indices owned by this
+        allocator. The result remains on the allocator device, avoiding a host
+        synchronization in the allocation or external-linker path. Zero means
+        a page has not received an identity. The snapshot fences stale control
+        completions; it is not a device-transfer termination receipt.
+        """
+        if indices.numel() == 0 or indices.numel() % self.page_size:
+            return None
+        if self._allocation_generations is None:
+            return None
+        page_ids = indices[:: self.page_size] // self.page_size
+        return torch.index_select(self._allocation_generations, 0, page_ids)
+
+    def allocation_generation_snapshot(
+        self, indices: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor | None, object | None]:
+        """Return page identities and the CUDA event that makes them ready."""
+        generations = self.allocation_generations(indices)
+        if generations is None or generations.device.type != "cuda":
+            return generations, None
+        ready = torch.cuda.Event()
+        ready.record(torch.cuda.current_stream(generations.device))
+        return generations, ready
